events.content:
Fixed. The title now appears immediately when navigating to the product page. **The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and that function calls `connection()`, which defers it to request time. With no Suspense boundary, Next.js couldn't send any of the page — even the static `

Premium Widget

` — until the inventory fetch finished, so navigation stalled on the slow data. **The fix:** I moved the fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in ``. The title is now part of the prerendered static shell and shows up instantly on navigation, while the stock count and price stream in behind a "Loading inventory..." fallback. The build confirms it: `/product` now reports as `◐ (Partial Prerender) — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content`, instead of fully dynamic.

content.text:
Fixed. The title now appears immediately when navigating to the product page. **The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top of the page component, and that function calls `connection()`, which defers it to request time. With no Suspense boundary, Next.js couldn't send any of the page — even the static `

Premium Widget

` — until the inventory fetch finished, so navigation stalled on the slow data. **The fix:** I moved the fetch into a child `Inventory` component and wrapped it in ``. The title is now part of the prerendered static shell and shows up instantly on navigation, while the stock count and price stream in behind a "Loading inventory..." fallback. The build confirms it: `/product` now reports as `◐ (Partial Prerender) — prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content`, instead of fully dynamic.
